title: Pulse
subtitle: Local AI coding agent for VS Code
description: A local offline AI coding agent for VS Code powered by Ollama. Pulse turns VS Code into a coding agent that can read your workspace, plan multi-step tasks, propose edits, run safe terminal commands, and remember prior work without sending your code to a cloud service.
problem: Cloud-based AI coding assistants send your code to external servers, raising privacy concerns and requiring constant internet connectivity. Developers in low-bandwidth environments need AI assistance that works entirely offline while still being capable of complex, multi-step coding tasks.
role: Designed and built the full VS Code extension from scratch — workspace-aware coding agent with file editing, terminal execution, session memory, and MCP server visibility. Implemented the sidebar UI with session history, model/provider controls, and the settings drawer.
approach: Built as a VS Code extension with a sidebar UI that communicates with a local Ollama instance. The agent uses workspace-aware context to understand project structure, implements role-based routing for different model capabilities, and maintains session memory with workspace+episodic memory modes. Includes performance profiling with adaptive quality targets.
hardestDecision: Choosing to route different agent roles (planner, editor, coder, reviewer) to different model sizes rather than using a single large model. This dramatically reduces VRAM requirements and improves response times, but adds complexity in managing model switching and ensuring consistency across roles.
outcome: Not yet published to VS Code Marketplace. Open source on GitHub with MIT license.
whatIdChange: Would implement streaming responses from agent stages earlier — the initial version used end-of-run replay which added unnecessary latency. Also would add more comprehensive protocol parsing tests from the start.
